strengths: Well-motivated problem formulation that elegantly articulates the gap between ML interpretability and clinical deployability, with explicit treatment of deployability as a hard constraint
Technically sound methodology combining LLM-guided proposal with deterministic validation; proper acknowledgment of NP-hardness with appropriate heuristic approach
Comprehensive evaluation spanning 8 tasks, 5-fold cross-validation, fair baseline comparisons with explicit constraints, and external validation against established clinical guidelines
External validation demonstrates practical value: outperforms SOFA/SAPS-I on ICU mortality and CF guidelines on transplant risk, with statistically significant improvements
Human-centered validation through clinician evaluation (N=18) showing strong preferences for AgentScore across guideline alignment, bedside ease, and deployment
Excellent contextual grounding with detailed survey of deployed clinical scoring systems and clinically-informed rule grammar with clear justification
Exceptional reproducibility through 38-page supplementary material with algorithms, hyperparameters, prompts, ablation studies; proper statistical testing with corrections
Honest and thorough limitations discussion; appropriate impact statement acknowledging research-only status and need for external validation
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—individual components (interpretable ML, LLM-guided search, score learning) are established; primary contribution is integration and problem formulation
Incomplete transparency on LLM-based clinical plausibility filtering: no quantitative analysis of rejection rates, failure modes, or potential introduction of subtle biases
Hyperparameter choices appear empirically motivated but lack systematic sensitivity analysis; key thresholds (auc_threshold=0.60, jaccard=0.9) justified informally with limited exploration
Code availability not mentioned despite LLM and reproducibility concerns; dependency on closed-source APIs (GPT-5, GPT-4o) limits long-term reproducibility and accessibility
External validation limited to only 2 tasks (ICU mortality, CF mortality); claims of generalizability not sufficiently supported across institutions and disease domains
Missing fairness and bias analysis for a clinical system: paper acknowledges potential for learning historical biases but provides no systematic fairness audit or subgroup validation
Baseline comparisons use coefficient constraint {-1,0,+1} across all methods; unclear if this is optimal comparison (what if baselines also allowed unit weights?)
Incomplete technical analysis: missing data handling (default to false) deserves deeper bias/variance analysis; temporal rule window selection appears fixed without sensitivity exploration
Limited explanation of why AgentScore outperforms stricter-constraint baselines; insufficient analysis of contributing factors (derived rules vs. search procedure)
Dense presentation (38 pages) with rule grammar overwhelming in appendix; combinatorial intractability argument somewhat disconnected from main narrative

strengths: Novel problem formulation: Treats deployability (memorability, auditability, bedside executability) as a hard modeling constraint rather than post-hoc consideration; unique focus on joint rule construction and selection

Well-motivated design choices: Unit-weighted checklists justified via cognitive science (Miller 1956), clinical practice (median 5 rules), and improper linear models; comprehensive clinically-grounded rule grammar

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 10 datasets (8 internal + 2 external), multiple baseline comparisons at different constraint levels, ablations isolating components, paired statistical tests, and clinician evaluation (N=18, 85% preference)
Principled LLM usage: Cleverly constrains LLMs to semantic proposal only, with all acceptance/rejection via deterministic data-grounded validation, mitigating hallucination risks
Strong empirical results: +0.031-0.109 AUROC improvements over score-learning baselines (p<0.001); higher discrimination than established guidelines (SOFA, SAPS-I) under external validation
Reproducibility and transparency: Detailed algorithms, full prompts, 25+ pages supplementary material, clear hyperparameter specification, code release announced, honest limitations discussion
weaknesses: Insufficient theoretical justification: Design choices (τ_rule=0.60, Jaccard threshold=0.95) lack deep justification with no sensitivity analysis; no formal convergence/approximation guarantees despite claiming to avoid NP-hardness; three-stage decomposition not proven optimal

Incomplete LLM analysis: Missing investigation of why LLM proposals work—no breakdown of proposal quality, rejection rates, or systematic rule discovery failures; Clinical Plausibility Agent underspecified and potential for introducing LLM bias not analyzed

Baseline fairness concerns: Optimal Checklists uses pre-specified features while AgentScore constructs semantic rules (conceptually different); representation-controlled ablations (E.2) partially address this but conflate rule generation quality with selection strategy; missing comparisons with recent LLM-guided feature generation methods

Limited external validation: Only 2 external cohorts (both from cystic fibrosis domain); validation within single healthcare system; no prospective real-world deployment (appropriately acknowledged but limits impact claims)

Computational dependency and reproducibility: ~220 API calls per fold at $1.12+; total cost >$500; dependence on proprietary frontier LLM models limits reproducibility; sustainability concerns for adoption

Incomplete clinical evaluation: Primary metric AUROC; formal calibration metrics (ECE, MCE) not reported for external validation; operating point considerations (sensitivity at fixed specificity) underemphasized; 18 clinicians with convenience sampling limits generalizability
Privacy claims overclaimed: Membership inference near chance (AUROC 0.509) is not a formal privacy guarantee; aggregate statistics can leak information; framed as more conclusive than warranted

Scope limitations underexplored: Applicability restricted to bedside N-of-M checklists (≤6 rules); many modern clinical decisions need richer models (continuous scores, treatment heterogeneity); insufficient discussion of when approach is/isn't appropriate
